text:
The text contrasts two perspectives on human nature. William Golding’s *Lord of the Flies* presents the theme that evil is inherent within humans, as evidenced by the boys' descent into savagery when removed from societal constraints. In contrast, Jean-Jacques Rousseau’s philosophy argues that society is the corrupting force, implying that humans are naturally good and free. The similarity lies in both works addressing the origin of human behavior and morality, but they differ fundamentally in their conclusions: Golding sees corruption as internal and innate, while Rousseau sees it as external and imposed by civilization.

The organ that pumps blood is the heart.
